perspectives.summary: Backup IDs and candidate cutoff are known, but Barman WAL continuity through 2026-08-21T02:47:22Z requires cloud-side read-only listing because Kubernetes metadata cannot close the historical archive gap.

Published Workspace Context S3 mode avoids an application-code change, but the target has no proven target-owned S3 path and no safe >=100Gi RWX path; existing NFS RWX PVs are bound and target restore is unproven.

Target OIDC discovery works, but SecretStore RBAC is missing and current mapping includes codicarium-users. Fresh target Data Protection, backend, runtime, MCP, and gateway credentials remain the safe default pending target-only approval.

pve-infra has no Workspace Context wrapper or artifact backend; existing published source chart/config has the required S3 contract and ExternalSecret hooks, so a wrapper can be considered only after storage and identity gates.

consensus_summary: Remain at spec. The published chart supports S3 without application changes, but source consistency evidence, target-owned artifact storage/restore, and target identity/secret decisions are still missing. No code, restore, reconciliation, live apply, source export, or Codicarium mutation is authorized.
open_questions: Will an ephemeral read-only Barman/S3 metadata path be provided?
Which distinct target-owned artifact backend is approved and recoverable without unapproved paid provisioning?
Should the target use a narrow homelab Authentik mapping and fresh target-only secrets/credentials?
Are the retained ownerless PVCs to remain preserved and untouched?
